content:
Label the nine points as a \(3\times 3\) grid:
\[
\begin{matrix}
A&B&C\\
D&E&F\\
G&H&I
\end{matrix}
\]

1. **At least three removals are necessary.**  
   Each horizontal row,
   \[
   \{A,B,C\},\qquad \{D,E,F\},\qquad \{G,H,I\},
   \]
   consists of three collinear points. Since these rows are disjoint, at least one point must be removed from each row. Thus at least \(3\) points must be removed.

2. **Three removals are sufficient.**  
   Remove \(A,E,I\), the three points on one main diagonal. The remaining points are
   \[
   B,C,D,F,G,H.
   \]
   Every row and column now contains only two remaining points. Of the two long diagonals, one has all its points removed, while the other has only two remaining points. These are all possible lines containing three points in a \(3\times3\) grid.

Therefore, the minimum number of points to remove is
\[
\boxed{3}.
\]
